farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾.
It came down concerning Māriya the Copt. The Prophet ﷺ used to assign a day to each of his wives. When it was ʿĀʾisha's day, Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar visited her, so her [Ḥafṣa's] house was empty, and the Prophet ﷺ sent for Māriya the Copt, and she was with the Prophet ﷺ in Ḥafṣa's dwelling. Ḥafṣa came to her dwelling and found the curtain let down. The Prophet ﷺ came out and said: Will you keep this secret for me? She said: Yes. He said: Then she is forbidden to me — meaning Māriya — and I tell you that your father and Abū Bakr will rule after me. Ḥafṣa told ʿĀʾisha the news, and revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ about it. He called Ḥafṣa and said: What made you do what you did? She said to him: And who told you that I said that to ʿĀʾisha? He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me". Then he divorced Ḥafṣa with one divorce and kept away from his wives for twenty-nine days. And there came down to him: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾, regarding intimacy with Māriya. Then He said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾, meaning: the expiation of your oaths. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed a slave and returned to Māriya.
[Al-Farrāʾ] said: Ḥibbān told me this interpretation from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Then He said: "عرف بعضه" — He is saying: he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of what was said and left part. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read "عَرَف", light.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Marwazī told me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī: "عَرَف", light.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: and a shaykh of Banū Asad — meaning al-Kisāʾī — told me, from Nuʿaym, from Abū ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: when a man recited to him "عَرَّف بعضه" with doubling, he would pelt him with pebbles. It is as if those who say عَرَف, light, mean: he was angered by it and requited it, as you say to a man who wrongs you: By Allah, I will surely "know" that against you (i.e. repay you for it). And by my life, he did requite Ḥafṣa by divorcing her; and this is a good interpretation. [And it is reported of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he read عَرَف light, like Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
This is a parable by which ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa are meant; He struck the parable for them both, saying: The faith of their husbands did not benefit the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, and their hypocrisy did not harm their husbands; likewise the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ would not benefit you two if you did not believe, and your sins would not harm him. Then He said: ﴿وضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلاً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْن﴾, so He commanded them both to be like Āsiya and like Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity (farj). Al-farj here is the neck-opening of her shift; it is mentioned that Jibrīl ﷺ blew into the opening of her garment. Every opening in a shift, whether a tear or otherwise, can be called farj. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَالَهَا مِنْ فُرُوجٍ﴾, meaning the sky has no cracks or rifts.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He means ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. That is because ʿĀʾisha said: O Messenger of Allah, as for the day of the others, you complete it, but on my day you do what you did? So there came down: "If you two repent to Allah" from your collaborating against the Prophet ﷺ ﴿فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾: they have deviated and inclined. ﴿وَإِن تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ﴾: [if] you collaborate against him. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it light, and the people of the Ḥijāz read it: "تظَّاهرا" with doubling. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ﴾: his protector against you both, ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: such as Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, in whom there is no hypocrisy. Then He said: ﴿وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾: after those, He means helpers, and He did not say ظهراء. If someone said that ظهير belongs to Jibrīl, the righteous believers and the angels [together], it would be correct; but it is good to make ظهير belong to the angels specifically, because of His saying (والملائكة) — after the help of these — [are] ظهير.
As for His saying: ﴿وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, it is singular in the sense of a plural, as you say: لا يأتينى إلا سائس الحرب (none shall come to me except the manager of war): whoever is capable of managing war has been told to come, whether one or more. Similar to it: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾: this is general [201/b], not one or two. Likewise His saying: ﴿والَّلذانِ يأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهما﴾, and likewise: ﴿إنّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾ and ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾ — in much of the Qurʾān the singular conveys the meaning of the plural.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read: "أنْ يُبْدلَهُ", light, and the people of the Ḥijāz read: "أن يبَدِّله" [with doubling]; and both are correct: أبدلت and بدّلت.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿سَائِحَاتٍ﴾.
They are women who fast. He said: We think that the one who fasts is called سائح (wanderer) only because the wanderer has no provisions with him and eats only where he finds [food], so it is as if it were taken from that. And Allah knows best.
The Arabs say of a horse when it stands without fodder: صائم (fasting). That is because it has two meals, a meal in the morning and a meal in the evening, so it is likened to the predawn meal of a human being and his breaking of the fast.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾.
Teach your families that by which they ward off sins; teach them that.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿تَوْبَةً نَّصُوحاً﴾.
The people of Medina and al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa on the nūn, and it is reported of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan [that they read] "نُصُوحاً" with ḍamma on the nūn. It is as if those who say "نُصوحاً" intend the maṣdar (verbal noun), like قُعودا, while those who say "نَصوحا" make it a description of the repentance. Its meaning is: when he repents of that sin, he resolves in himself never to return to it.
His saying: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾.
Not everyone who enters Paradise says this; only the lowest of them in rank says it. That is because the foremost, as has been mentioned, pass over the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) like lightning, some like the wind, some like a swift horse, and some crawling and creeping. It is these who say: ﴿رَبَّنَا أتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾ so that we may be saved.
If a reader read "ويدخلْكم" in the jussive, it would be a valid way, because the answer [is] to عسى: the فاء is implied in [the answer to] عسى, and "entering" is intended as conjoined to the place of the فاء. But no one read it so. Similar to it: ﴿فَأَصَّدَقَ وأكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِين﴾.
Similar is the poet's saying:
فأبلونى بليتكُم لعلى * أصالحكم، واستدرجْ نَويَّا
(So grant me your favour, perhaps I may make peace with you, and draw my distant company [back] step by step.)
He put it in the jussive because he intended joining it back to لعلّى.
